title: ScoutBridge POC initiation — kickoff ops notes & success checklist
body:
Purpose:
This doc captures operational kickoff notes, technical assumptions, acceptance criteria, and next steps for the ScoutBridge POC (customer: ScoutBridge Analytics). The goal is to validate Redwood Dedicated deployment patterns for a low-latency semantic search + summarization workflow and to define clear success gates for a 6-week engagement.

Summary of kickoff (2024-11-15):
- Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood SE lead), Ethan Park (infra), Ravi Patel (applied ML), Lina Gomez (customer eng, ScoutBridge), Sofia Martinez (security).
- Customer use case: ingest customer support transcripts, build embeddings and vector index, serve search and on-demand extractive summarization for agent assist. Expected steady-state traffic: 30–80 QPS during business hours, peak 150 RPS during campaigns.
- Core ask: demonstrate Dedicated GPU pool serving a quantized LLM for summarization + smaller embedding model for retrieval, with transparent cost and latency SLAs, and an integration pattern for ScoutBridge’s existing ingestion pipeline.

Technical assumptions & constraints:
- Data residency: all transcript text remains in customer's VPC (private deployment) until indexing; only tokens for model inference cross service boundary under customer-managed network peering.
- Model choices (provisional): embedder: small-embed-v2 (float16), reranker: cross-ranker-lite, summarizer: redwood-mini-7B-quant (8-bit PTQ). Final model selection depends on early quality tests in week 1.
- Infrastructure: Dedicated cluster with 4x A100-80GB nodes, autoscale + burst to 6 nodes allowed for peak. Node access via private control plane.
- Integration: ScoutBridge will forward batched requests to Redwood routing endpoint; initial approach uses prefix caching for repeated summaries and automatic KV cache kept warm for long-running sessions.
- Security: KMS-managed keys (customer AWS KMS), TLS mutual auth between services, audit logs forwarded to customer Splunk instance.

Workshop agenda notes (kickoff -> week 1):
1) Architecture walkthrough (15m): outline data flow, control plane interactions, and network setup.
2) Data onboarding checklist (30m): what files, format, PII markers, sample size for embedding tests.
3) Model & eval plan (30m): define prompt templates, quality metrics, and sample tests.
4) Performance and capacity targets (20m): agree p95/p99 latency targets and throughput targets.
5) Risk and rollback playbook (15m): fallback models, rate limits, and fail-open vs fail-closed strategies.

Acceptance criteria (POC success gates):
- Functional (must meet):
  - Ingestion: pipeline can ingest 10K transcripts and produce embeddings within 24 hours without data loss.
  - Retrieval correctness: top-5 precision >= 0.88 on spot-check set of 200 queries.
  - Summarization quality: ROUGE-L relative improvement >= 18% vs baseline heuristic summarizer on sampled transcripts.
- Performance (must meet):
  - Summarization latency (server-side): p95 <= 450 ms for 512-token outputs; p99 <= 900 ms during steady-state load (30–80 QPS).
  - Embedding latency: p95 <= 60 ms per item when batched (batch sizes 64–128).
  - Availability: system error rate < 1% over a continuous 72-hour validation window, and successful failover to fallback model with < 5s additional latency.
- Cost & ops (should meet):
  - Unit cost: estimated inference cost <= $0.45 per 1k tokens for summarization at steady-state when employing caching/batching optimizations.
  - Observability: per-request token-level cost and latency visible in Redwood Console for all test traffic.
- Security & compliance (must meet):
  - No transcript data persisted outside customer-managed VPC without explicit opt-in.
  - KMS integration validated and test encryption keys rotated successfully in staging.

Roles & responsibilities:
- Redwood SE (Maya Chen): POC owner; coordinate model selection, lead evals, and drive acceptance checklist.
- Redwood Infra (Ethan Park): Dedicated cluster setup, networking (VPC peering), autoscaling policies.
- Applied ML (Ravi Patel): embedding and summarization quality evaluation, prompt tuning.
- Customer (Lina Gomez + ScoutBridge eng): provide sample data, ensure test harness deployed, verify downstream UI integration.
- Security (Sofia Martinez): run security checklist and review audit logs and key management.

Preliminary deployment topology (notes):
- Private control plane in Redwood account; compute nodes in customer VPC via dedicated tenancy.
- Ingestion -> preprocessor (customer) -> S3 (encrypted) -> batch embed job -> vector DB (customer-managed) -> Redwood Dedicated endpoints for re-ranking + summarization via private endpoint.
- Caching: prefix-level KV cache for session-owner conversations with TTL 12 hours; summary cache for identical doc IDs to avoid re-generation.

Integration checklist (initial):
- [ ] Sample dataset (500–1000 transcripts) delivered to S3 bucket by 2024-11-18 (owner: Lina).
- [ ] Network peering and firewall rules approved and tested (owner: Ethan) target: 2024-11-21.
- [ ] KMS test key created and rotated once in staging (owner: Sofia) target: 2024-11-20.
- [ ] Test harness for synthetic QPS load (30/80/150 RPS scenarios) validated (owner: Maya) target: 2024-11-22.
- [ ] Initial prompt templates and eval rubric in Confluence (owner: Ravi) target: 2024-11-19.

Known risks and mitigation:
- Risk: Embedding precision underperforms on domain-specific jargon (risk: medium). Mitigation: quick fine-tuning with 5k domain examples or fall back to hybrid lexical+semantic retrieval.
- Risk: Network egress throttling during peak ingest (risk: medium-high). Mitigation: schedule heavy ingestion out of business hours and pre-warm caches; enable burst nodes.
- Risk: Summary hallucinations for long transcripts (risk: medium). Mitigation: apply retrieval-augmented summarization and conservative temperature settings; add unit tests for factuality.

Open questions captured in kickoff:
- Customer retention of raw transcripts: confirm retention window (asked by Lina, pending).
- Exact SLA required for p99 latency after go-live (requested by customer PM; default POC target set to p99 <= 900 ms).
- Will customer accept managed vector DB or insist on fully self-hosted vector store?

Immediate action items (owners & due dates):
- Maya: finalize model shortlist and spawn quality eval job (due 2024-11-18).
- Ethan: provision Dedicated cluster skeleton and validate peering (due 2024-11-21).
- Ravi: prepare eval rubric and the 200-query spot-check set (due 2024-11-19).
- Lina: deliver sample dataset and provide list of PII fields to redact (due 2024-11-18).
- Sofia: run initial threat model for ingress/egress patterns and share findings (due 2024-11-20).

Success celebration criteria (post-POC):
- If all must-meet acceptance criteria satisfied and customer signs off on integration timeline, propose a 12-week pilot conversion to Redwood Dedicated with estimated committed capacity (recommended starting commit: 4x A100).
- If functional metrics met but ops/cost targets need tuning, propose a second-phase optimization sprint (2 weeks) focused on quantization and batching improvements.

Appendix: quick checklist for the validation window (72 hours)
- Deploy test harness -> ramp to 30 QPS steady for 24h -> capture p95/p99 and error rates -> ramp to 80 QPS for 12h -> run 3x peak bursts (150 RPS) and validate failover.
- Collect 2,000 sample requests to feed into quality eval pipeline; annotate 200 with gold summaries.

Notes to self:
- Keep prompts consistent across runs to avoid prompt variation noise when comparing models.
- Prioritize caching config that doesn't compromise freshness for agent-assist flows.

References & links:
- Confluence architecture draft: confluence:SB-POC-architecture
- Jira epic: SE-3987 (POC: ScoutBridge)
